newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Scientific Games downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Scientific Games downgraded.

text.p: Salomon Brothers analysts Bruce Turner and Beth Roberts lowered their rating on Scientific Games Holding Corp's stock to hold from buy, the firm said.
-- The analysts cut their 1997 earnings estimate to $1.68 a share from $1.80 and their 1998 view to $1.70 from $2.15.
-- They said the downgrade was related to the company's statement Thursday that it had been awarded a five-year extension of its cooperative services contract with the Georgia Lottery Corp.
-- The company said its rate of compensation for the remainder of the contract term and the extension is about 2.4 percent of instant lottery sales, reduced from the current 3.2 percent of sales.
-- The Salomon analysts said the change led them to reduce their 1997 earnings forecast by $0.11 a share and the 1988 estimate by $0.25.
-- They made further reductions to estimates to reflect slower-than-expected roll-out for the company's SciScan keyless validation systems.
-- "Scientific Games continues to be hindered by pricing pressures in the heightened competitive environment," they said in a research report issued Friday.
-- The stock was off 5/8 to 19-3/4 early Friday afternoon.
